captions.search.notFound: The {side} branch of {node} is empty, so {key} is not in the tree.
captions.insert.root: The tree is empty, so {key} becomes the root.
captions.insert.place: {key} goes in the empty {side} branch of {parent}.
captions.imbalance.insert: Node {node} has balance factor {bf}: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case {case} ({code}).
captions.imbalance.delete: Node {node} has balance factor {bf}: it is unbalanced.
captions.done: Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
captions.inorderCheck: In-order before: {before}. After: {after}. The BST order is unchanged.
captions.format: Numbers use a true minus sign (−). A negative height inside a subtraction is bracketed: 3 − (−1).

search-loop: if element in node p equals el
return element in node p  // el was found
else if el < element in node p
return null  // el was not found
search-recursive: return null  // end of tree reached
else if element in root equals el
return element in root  // el was found
else if el < element in root

glossary.root: The top node of a tree. It has no parent.
glossary.height: The number of edges on the longest path from a node down to a leaf. A leaf has height 0; an empty branch has height −1.
glossary.balance factor: bf = height of the right branch − height of the left branch.
glossary.AVL tree: A binary search tree in which every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
glossary.n: The first unbalanced node found on the way back up after an insertion.
glossary.rotation: A local change that moves a child up around its parent without changing the in-order sequence.
glossary.single rotation: One left or right rotation. Fixes the outside cases (1 and 4).
glossary.double rotation: Two rotations: first about a child of n, then about n. Fixes the inside cases (2 and 3).
glossary.in-order traversal: Visit the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. In a BST this lists the keys in sorted order.
glossary.outside case: The new key went into the left subtree of n’s left child (Case 1) or the right subtree of n’s right child (Case 4).
glossary.inside case: The new key went into the right subtree of n’s left child (Case 2) or the left subtree of n’s right child (Case 3).
glossary.O(log n): Grows like the number of times n can be halved. For 1,000,000 keys, log₂ n ≈ 20.

questionTypes.mcq: Multiple choice; every wrong option names a misconception and has its own explanation.
questionTypes.case-id: Multiple choice over the four cases; options and the correct case come from the engine.
questionTypes.enter-values: The student enters heights or balance factors for the target nodes.
questionTypes.click-node: The student clicks a node (target: first-unbalanced, all-violations or parent-of-new-key).
questionTypes.trace: The student clicks the search path, then Found or Not found.
questionTypes.perform-rotation: The student sees the tree right after the BST step and performs the rotation(s).
questionTypes.build-tree: The student carries out the operation(s), including rebalancing, and builds the final tree.

wrongAnswerPatterns.goes-wrong-direction: A trace step goes left for a larger key or right for a smaller key.
wrongAnswerPatterns.visits-extra-nodes: A trace includes a node that is not on the search path.
wrongAnswerPatterns.rotated-at-root: The student rotates about the root when n is lower down.
wrongAnswerPatterns.rotated-wrong-direction: The student rotates the opposite way (left instead of right, or the reverse).
wrongAnswerPatterns.double-wrong-order: For an inside case, the student rotates about n first, or about the wrong child.
wrongAnswerPatterns.rotated-again-above-n: After fixing n, the student also rotates an ancestor of n.
